content:
I can’t place orders or be your legally responsible portfolio manager, but I can give you a concrete, low-maintenance decision you can run yourself.

## Decision: 70% global equities / 30% CHF short-term government bonds

Assumption: you don’t need to withdraw this money before roughly age 65, and you can tolerate a serious market drop of 25–40%. If you need withdrawals sooner or want much more stability, increase the short-bond/cash portion.

## First trades now

| # | Action | Instrument | ISIN / ticker | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | **Sell** | Any existing holdings that are not already broad, low-cost global equity ETFs or CHF short-term government bond funds: single stocks, sector/thematic funds, crypto, leveraged products, concentrated positions, duplicate ETFs. | — | 100% of those holdings |
| 2 | **Buy** | **Vanguard FTSE All-World UCITS ETF (USD) Accumulating** — broad global developed + emerging markets, large/mid/small caps, low cost. | **IE00BK5BQT80** / ticker **VWRL** where listed | **CHF 280,000** |
| 3 | **Buy** | **iShares 1–3 Year CHF Government Bond UCITS ETF (Acc)** — short-duration CHF government bond buffer. If your broker does not list it, use an equivalent CHF 1–3 year government bond ETF or CHF money-market fund. | **IE00B9V58T07** / ticker **IHSF** where listed | **CHF 120,000** |
| 4 | **Do** | Leave only rounding cash in the brokerage account. | — | ~CHF 0 |

If the account is already cash, skip the sell step and make the two buys. If you already hold these ETFs, just top them up to the 70/30 weights.

## Execution

- Use limit orders near market.
- Do not wait for a dip.
- If sells and buys cannot settle same-day, sell first, then buy when cash settles.
- If your broker charges high FX fees on the USD-denominated equity ETF, use a CHF-quoted equivalent broad global equity ETF instead.

## Ongoing rule

No ad-hoc trades. Rebalance only:

- once per year, or
- if the equity allocation moves outside **65%–75%**.

When rebalancing:

- If equity is above 75%, sell equity and buy the bond ETF back to 70/30.
- If equity is below 65%, sell bonds and buy the equity ETF back to 70/30.

Do not market-time or panic-sell during drawdowns. The 30% bond sleeve is the buffer; the 70% equity sleeve is the growth engine.
